details.releaseNotesExcerpt: ## New Models ### Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Mistral Large 4 is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe. Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> metal : faster MXFP4 mat-vec, full threadgroups for unary/binary/GLU (#31075) * metal : faster MXFP4 mat-vec kernel Decode the fp4 values with the fp16 bit trick instead of a threadgroup lookup table, and load the packed nibbles as aligned 32-bit words. The kernel no longer uses threadgroup memory. * metal : launch contiguous unary and binary ops with full threadgroups The contiguous unary path and the row-broadcast binary path used one thread per threadgroup. Use up to 256 threads per threadgroup and bound-check the tail. * metal : split GLU rows across threadgroups A GLU row ran on one threadgroup, so single-row decode used a single threadgroup for the whole op. Split each row over threadgroups of up to 256 threads. </details> **Website:** - <https://llama.app> **Attestations:** - <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/61399679> **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11985/llama-b11985-bin-ma
